items.summary: Recommendation: preserve containment-only execution and retain three deferred, evidence-backed opportunities for later CEO/CTO review; create no proposal, experiment, change request, telemetry request, dependency adoption, spend, or deployment this cycle. 1) deeppenetrations.com liquid-wrench search capture: use-case is a tightly scoped review-page title/meta/FAQ and internal-link refinement; evidence is 91 impressions, position 2.8, 0 clicks, versus a 10.0% conservative CTR target; metric is organic CTR/clicks with affiliate clicks secondary; time-to-learn is the existing measurement window; smallest reversible prototype is metadata plus one contextual link, with rollback by reverting those fields. Risks: no revenue or causal lift is established, affiliate attribution is partial-aggregate, and the site currently has active measurement work. 2) broadwayshowgirls.com Priya Raghunathan search capture: use-case is a focused author-page title/description and search-intent content refinement; evidence is 61 impressions, position 2, 0 clicks, versus a 15.0% conservative CTR target; metric is organic CTR/clicks and downstream sessions; time-to-learn is the existing measurement window; smallest reversible prototype is metadata and one above-fold clarification, rolled back by reverting the page copy. Risks: no conversion or revenue evidence, and the site has existing queued/measuring work. 3) americastrikes.com mobile performance: use-case is reducing render-blocking assets and JavaScript on the measured landing surface; evidence is mobile performance 64, LCP 4,789ms, and TBT 700ms; metric is LCP/TBT and organic engagement, not financial return; time-to-learn is one controlled validation plus the existing measurement window; smallest reversible prototype is one isolated asset-loading or script-deferral change with a revert path. Risks: security/release evidence is incomplete, prior implementation failures remain under containment, and performance metrics do not establish revenue. GitHub signals remain discovery-only: shadcn-ui/ui and microsoft/markitdown are MIT and passed bounded lab checks, while mermaid-js/mermaid is MIT but had no safe native checks; adoption risks include dependency provenance, maintenance, bundle/security review, and owner-approved implementation. No repository should be added until prototype, security review, measurement capacity, and approval gates clear. Preserve attribution guardrails: the 2026-09-21 Amazon record shows $4.92 aggregate commission and $0 site-attributed commission; do not infer ROI, conversion lift, margin, payback, or revenue upside.
